title: Worktree-Isolated Parallel Agents
intent: gzkit runs one agent at a time against the working tree; it has no isolation substrate for concurrent agent work. Two external tools — swarm-forge (Robert C. Martin) and superpowers (Jesse Vincent) — both get parallel agents essentially for free by giving each agent its own git worktree. This pool ADR captures adopting that substrate. The PRIMARY motivating use case is deliberately the SAFEST one: parallel review personas — run spec-reviewer, quality-reviewer, and other review subagents concurrently against one change. That mode is read-only fan-out (reviewers produce findings, not ledger events), so it needs only worktree isolation and does NOT depend on the ledger-concurrency substrate. Write-heavy modes (parallel OBPI implementation, parallel GHI fixes) are recorded as future scope and depend on ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate.
decision:
1. Adopt EPHEMERAL git worktrees as the isolation substrate: scratch checkouts (e.g. under `.worktrees/<slug>`), each with its own clean baseline, NEVER pushed as a remote branch, landing on `main` via fast-forward/squash at merge.
2. This preserves the intent of the standing operator directive 'Never create feature branches — work directly on main', which bans the PR/squash-merge/delete BRANCH DANCE, not physical scratch checkouts. Promotion of this ADR REQUIRES an operator-ratified doctrine carve-out amending that directive to permit ephemeral worktrees explicitly.
3. Primary mode (lands first): parallel READ-ONLY review personas. gzkit already owns the review topology (spec-reviewer + quality-reviewer subagents — the same two-stage 'spec compliance then code quality' shape superpowers ships); only the worktree substrate that lets them run concurrently against clean baselines is new.
4. Write-heavy modes (deferred, dependent): parallel OBPI implementation under one ADR; parallel independent GHI fixes; parallel ADR pipelines. Each depends on ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate (single-writer-by-construction) to keep Layer-2 consistent.
5. Worktrees are Layer-3 scratch: nothing in a worktree is source-of-truth until it merges to main (state-doctrine).
positive_consequences:
1. gzkit gains true parallel agent execution — a capability it provably lacks today and both credited tools have.
2. The primary (read-only review) mode is safe to land WITHOUT the substrate ADR, because reviewers write no Layer-2 events — fast first value.
3. Isolation is by construction (separate worktrees), so parallel agents cannot stomp each other's working tree — the failure mode swarm-forge designed out.
4. Reuses gzkit's existing review-persona subagents; no new review methodology, only concurrency.
5. Preserves 'everything lands on main': ephemeral worktrees fast-forward into the single main lane, no branch dance.
negative_consequences:
1. Requires amending a standing operator directive (no feature branches). Without the ratified carve-out this ADR cannot promote — a hard governance gate, not a technical one.
2. Worktree lifecycle is new operational surface: creation, clean-baseline verification, merge, teardown, and orphan cleanup (a crashed agent leaves a stale `.worktrees/<slug>`).
3. Write-heavy modes are only as safe as ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate; shipping them before that substrate would reintroduce the ledger race.
4. Read-only review fan-out has a subtle sync hazard: reviewers must pin the SAME commit, or they review divergent trees and produce non-comparable findings.
5. Disk and setup cost per worktree (superpowers/swarm-forge both note this) — parallelism trades disk + setup latency for wall-clock.
checklist:
1. Author + ratify the doctrine carve-out permitting ephemeral worktrees (operator-gated; blocks promotion).
2. Worktree lifecycle manager: create `.worktrees/<slug>` from a pinned commit, verify clean test baseline, tear down on completion, reap orphans.
3. Read-only review-persona fan-out: dispatch N review subagents concurrently against one pinned commit; collect findings. (Independent of the substrate ADR.)
4. Merge-to-main path for worktree output: fast-forward/squash onto main; no remote branch.
5. Write-heavy modes (parallel OBPI impl / GHI fixes / ADR pipelines) — deferred; each gated on ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate.
alternatives:
1. Separate full clones per agent instead of worktrees: REJECTED — heavier (full clone per agent), and merging back across clones is more complex than a worktree fast-forward. Worktrees share one object store.
2. Single shared working tree with advisory locks / turn-taking: REJECTED — that is the status quo (no real parallelism) plus a race; it is exactly what worktree isolation removes.
3. Decline worktrees; borrow only the coordination-substrate ideas: REJECTED as the capability ADR (it is the substrate ADR ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate instead). Recorded because the operator noted parallelism itself is not the main draw — but the read-only review fan-out is cheap enough to be worth the substrate.

forcing_functions.pre_mortem: 18 months on, this failed because ephemeral worktrees were adopted WITHOUT the doctrine carve-out being ratified first, so an agent's `.worktrees/<slug>` got pushed as a remote branch during a git-sync, reintroducing the exact branch-dance the operator banned. Mitigation: checklist item 1 is a hard promotion gate; the merge path (item 4) must be push-to-main-only with no branch publish.
forcing_functions.wwhtbt: For worktree isolation to be the right substrate, it must be true that gzkit's parallel work decomposes into independent units that rarely touch the same files. Shakiest condition: two review personas or two OBPI implementations that DO overlap heavily — then isolation just defers a merge conflict. Judged acceptable because the primary mode is read-only (no merge at all) and OBPI decomposition already aims for independent briefs.
forcing_functions.reversibility: Two-way door for the read-only review mode (delete `.worktrees/`, revert to serial review — no persistent state). Closer to one-way for the doctrine carve-out: once 'ephemeral worktrees allowed' is canon, un-ratifying it after workflows depend on it is expensive. Sequencing (carve-out gated at promotion) keeps the reversible part reversible.
forcing_functions.operator_2am: On-call at 2am, three worktrees are half-merged and one agent crashed leaving a dirty `.worktrees/impl-b`. The operator needs: one command listing every worktree, its pinned commit, merge state, and whether it holds unmerged work; and a safe teardown that never discards unmerged commits. Checklist item 2 owes this.
forcing_functions.scope_minimization: Smallest valuable version: the read-only review-persona fan-out (checklist items 2 + 3) with the doctrine carve-out (item 1). That alone delivers 'run all reviewers in parallel against a clean baseline' and needs NO ledger-concurrency work. The write-heavy modes (items 4-5) wait for the substrate ADR.
forcing_functions.downstream_adrs: Forces the doctrine carve-out amendment (operator-ratified). Depends on ADR-pool.ledger-concurrency-substrate for write-heavy modes. May force a worktree-lifecycle feature ADR and a `gz worktree` CLI surface ADR at promotion.
